_readme: Named look presets. Pick one with RUFUS_STYLE=<name>; the text is used as
the stills detail suffix, exactly as if it had been pasted into
RUFUS_STILLS_DETAIL. A literal RUFUS_STILLS_DETAIL still wins over a
preset name, so a one-off experiment never has to be added here first.
These are LOOKS, not subjects. The niche decides what the video is about;
a style decides how it is drawn. money_history rendered as stickman is a
different channel from money_history rendered flat-vector, and neither
needs a change to the research, the script or the storyboard.
A style has to be describable in ONE block of text that is appended to
every prompt byte for byte. That is not a limitation of this file — it is
how look consistency works at all: an image model renders each beat from
noise with no memory of the others, so two paraphrases of one style are
stickman: Minimalist stick-figure cartoon illustration drawn in thin, clean black line art of uniform weight. Every figure has a perfect oval head slightly taller than wide with a white fill and a thin black outline, two solid black oval dot eyes evenly spaced in the upper-middle third of the face, two short straight eyebrow strokes above them, and one thin curved line for the mouth — and nothing else: no nose, no ears, no cheek lines, no hair, completely bald and smooth. THE FACE CARRIES THE EMOTION OF THE MOMENT and must not be the same on every figure: brows angled down and inward over a flat or down-curved mouth for anger, brows raised high over a small open oval mouth for shock, brows slanted up at their inner ends over a downward mouth curve for worry or grief, a wide upturned curve with the eyes squeezed to short arcs for delight, brows flat and mouth a short straight line for cold indifference. The pose carries it too: shoulders thrown up, arms reaching, back hunched, head dropped, one figure leaning away from another. The body is stick-figure: one straight line for the torso, thin straight arms angled at the elbow, thin straight legs angled at the knee, small simple hands, no muscle lines, no filled body mass, no volume. A single thin vertical line for the neck. Clothing is drawn as simple line-art garments with flat unshaded colour fills inside the outlines only. ANIMALS AND OBJECTS ARE DRAWN PROPERLY, and this contrast is the whole charm of the style: the PEOPLE stay simple stick figures, while an animal, a machine, a ship or a building is a real illustration with its true shape, proportions and markings — a zebra has its stripes and mane, a lion its mane and tail tuft, a coin its rim, a cart its wheels and boards. Same clean black outline, same flat saturated fills, but drawn with care and detail a stick figure never gets. BEHIND THE FIGURES, BUILD THE WHOLE PLACE. Every frame is a complete scene, not a figure floating on paper: a ground plane filling the bottom third to half of the frame, a horizon line across it, and open sky above. On the ground and along the horizon go the four to eight things that say where this is — hills, a river bank, bushes and grass tufts, a stone wall, market stalls, rooftops, ship masts, machinery, crates, bones and stones scattered in the dirt. Draw them in the same clean black line art as everything else. COLOUR IS FLAT, SATURATED AND REAL: grass is green, sky is a clear light blue with a few simple white clouds, earth and sand are warm brown, water is blue, stone is grey. Fill every shape with solid colour edge to edge. Never wash the background out, never draw it paler or thinner than the foreground, and never leave it as bare paper — a scene where only the figure is finished looks unfinished. The background is quieter than the subject because it is simpler and further away, not because it is faded. THE PLACE PERSISTS: consecutive shots in one location keep the same horizon height, the same colours and the same landmarks, so the sequence reads as one world seen from different angles rather than a new drawing each time. No gradients, no shading, no ambient occlusion, no texture, no photographic lighting, no depth of field, no film grain. Bold, readable silhouettes; the whole frame reads instantly at thumbnail size.
flat_vector: Flat 2D vector illustration style, not a photograph: clean confident outlines of consistent stroke weight, simplified geometric shapes rendered in flat, unshaded color fills. No gradients, no photographic lighting, no film grain, no lens blur or depth of field, no skin pores or fabric-weave texture. Figures and objects are graphic and stylized rather than anatomically photographic — bold silhouettes, minimal internal linework, an expressive pose read through shape and posture. Lighting is rendered as bold graphic contrast — a hard-edged light shape or color-block shadow — never a soft photographic gradient. Backgrounds simplify into clean shapes and generous negative space rather than photographic clutter. Reads like modern explainer-video or storybook illustration: crisp, deliberate, and stylized, never a photograph or a photo-real render. BUILD THE WHOLE SCENE, never a subject floating on blank paper: a ground plane filling the lower third to half of the frame, a horizon across it, sky above, and the four to eight things that say where this is. Colour is FLAT and SATURATED and fills every shape edge to edge — no gradients, no shading, no ambient occlusion, no texture, no photographic lighting, no depth of field, no film grain. The background is quieter than the subject because it is simpler and further away, never because it is faded or paler. Consecutive shots in one place keep the same horizon height, colours and landmarks. Bold, readable silhouettes; the whole frame reads instantly at thumbnail size.
ink_woodcut: Monochrome ink woodcut engraving, the look of a 19th-century newspaper illustration. Dense parallel hatching and cross-hatching for every tone; no grey fills, no gradients, no colour. Heavy confident contour lines, fine interior hatching, deep blacks against untouched white paper. Slight plate texture and ink bleed at the line edges. Figures are solid and weighty, drawn with anatomical confidence rather than stylisation. Reads like a printed engraving lifted from an 1890s broadsheet.
paper_cut: Paper-cutout collage illustration, as if every element were scissored from sheets of coloured construction paper and laid in layers. Each shape is a clean flat silhouette with a slightly rough torn or cut edge and a soft drop shadow one or two pixels down and right, so the layers read as real paper stacked on paper. People are simple rounded cutout figures with dot eyes and a single curved mouth line, their limbs separate paper pieces. Warm saturated palette: mustard yellow, tomato red, teal, cream and deep navy, with the sky a single flat sheet. Objects and animals are cut with care and keep their real proportions and markings. BUILD THE WHOLE SCENE, never a subject floating on blank paper: a ground plane filling the lower third to half of the frame, a horizon across it, sky above, and the four to eight things that say where this is. The background is quieter than the subject because it is simpler and further away, never because it is faded or paler. Consecutive shots in one place keep the same horizon height, colours and landmarks. Bold, readable silhouettes; the whole frame reads instantly at thumbnail size.
chalkboard: White and pastel chalk drawing on a deep slate-green board. Every line is a slightly grainy chalk stroke with soft edges and visible texture where the chalk caught the board, and the board itself shows faint smudges and eraser sweeps in the empty areas. People are simple chalk stick figures with dot eyes and drawn brows. Accents in dusty yellow, coral, sky blue and mint, used sparingly against the white. Diagrams, arrows and simple labelled shapes are welcome — this is the look of a good teacher mid-explanation. Objects and animals are drawn properly with real proportions. retro_print: 1950s screen-printed poster illustration in a limited four-colour palette: burnt orange, mustard, sage green and off-black on warm cream stock. Bold confident outlines of varying weight, shapes filled with flat ink and the occasional coarse halftone dot field where a mid-tone is needed, plus a deliberate one-or-two-pixel misregistration on some fills as though a plate slipped. People are simple stylised figures with strong silhouettes and minimal faces. Mid-century geometric shapes: long shadows, simplified architecture, stylised clouds and hills. storybook: Children's picture-book illustration in soft gouache: hand-painted flat shapes with a visible brushed edge, gentle warm colours — butter yellow, sage, dusty rose, cornflower blue, soft brown — and a thin uneven ink line over the top on the important shapes only. People are simple round-headed figures with dot eyes, drawn brows and a single mouth line, warm and friendly. Animals and objects are painted with real care and keep their true shapes and markings. Everything is calm, generous and a little hand-made; nothing is mechanical or vector-perfect.
